Hi Samantha / Helix procurement team,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. We reviewed the draft Order Form and MSA exhibit and want to lock down two operational points before legal redlines:

1) Evidence "deadbands" (windows where we won't accept rolling evidence requests) — Helix proposed continuous access; we need to propose realistic windows to protect multi-tenant operations.
2) Pen-test gating & staging access — clarify notice timing, staff escalation path, and ephemeral creds for the test window.

Can you confirm the earliest acceptable inspection windows for Helix (target months or quarters) and whether your security team needs an on-premise forensic-access option or will accept our staging snapshot approach?

I'm attaching our suggested Order Form edits (high level) and a SOC 2 coverage summary so your team can map requests to assertions. Proposed next steps:
- Helix confirms acceptable deadband periods (example: two 72-hour windows per quarter).
- Redwood proposes a pen-test notice cadence (30 days notice, 7-day blackout before production cutover).
- Legal teams exchange redlines; we aim to finalize before procurement signature.

If helpful, Ben and Laura are on standby to do a quick review call.

Thanks,

Michael Grant

Michael — thanks for the note and the attachments. Quick answers from Helix security / procurement:

- Deadbands: we prefer discrete scheduled windows rather than continuous open access. Two 72-hour windows per quarter is acceptable as a starting point; we can be flexible if you can commit to a fixed calendar.
- Pen-test gating: 30 days notice is fine. We require ephemeral credentialing and a staging snapshot for tests that could affect PHI-handling flows. For high-impact tests we reserve the right to request a forensic snapshot post-test.
- Forensic-access: we'd rather avoid on-prem unless strictly necessary. Staging snapshot + audit logs should be acceptable if you provide clear chain-of-custody documentation.

Procurement will need the exact Order Form language for the evidence cadence and a clarified Exhibit so they can circulate to legal. I'll attach Helix's preferred redline examples after I sync with our counsel (ETA tomorrow).

—Samantha
Head of Security Programs
Helix Health

Looping internal legal ops considerations — flagged items for our redline: 

1) Deadband definition — avoid ambiguous language. Propose exact calendar examples and a clause that limits evidence requests outside scheduled windows to documented incidents with SOC2-relevant severity.
2) Forensic snapshot ransom / data-protection language — require Helix to specify the scope and provide written consent for any snapshot that could include customer data.
3) Staging credentialing — recommend technical controls: ephemeral keys (rotated by us), read-only accounts for Helix testers, and a single named point of contact for escalation.

I'll draft the proposed exhibit text this afternoon and attach a one-page table that crosswalks each evidence item to SOC2 assertion and our proposed access cadence. Laura — if you can check procurement impacts (billing / SLA triggers tied to evidence windows) that would be great.

Samantha — thanks, appreciate the quick turnaround. Per our internal review we've prepared a proposed exhibit paragraph and an operational runbook (summary below). I've attached the redline PDF (OrderForm_HLX_v2_redline.pdf) and SOC2 mapping. Key points: 

- Deadbands: "Helix will be allocated two scheduled evidence windows per fiscal quarter (each up to 72 hours). Requests for additional evidence access outside these windows are limited to incident response with acceptable threshold language (defined in appendix A)."

- Pen-test gating: "Helix will provide 30 days notice. Redwood will provision ephemeral test credentials and a staging snapshot with a maximum of 48 hours access for active tests. For forensic snapshots post-test, Helix must request explicit written consent and narrow scope to affected systems."

- Chain-of-custody and logs: Redwood will provide a signed chain-of-custody manifest for any snapshot, and standard audit logs (30 days retention by default). Extended retention or special handling will be a billable add-on.

Next steps:
- Samantha: confirm Helix counsel's preferred language for incident threshold in appendix A (you mentioned sending examples).
- Procurement: if the operational constraints look good, we can exchange formal redlines between legal teams and prepare for signature.

If Helix is OK, I'll ask Legal to circulate a tracked redline of the MSA exhibit by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
